newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Credit says talk of its collapse groundless.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Credit says talk of its collapse groundless.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd said on Wednesday that vague rumours in the financial market that the bank was on the verge of collapse, which prompted sales of the bank's shares and debentures, were "totally groundless".

"In the markets, unsourced rumours such as the suggestion that our bank is practically on the verge of collapse are circulating and are prompting sales of our shares and debentures. Such rumours are totally groundless and our bank would like to declare that these rumours are not true," the bank said in a statement.
The bank's operations are normal, with ample funds, so the bank has no worries about its business, it said.
On Nippon Credit's business results for the year ending in March, it said its operating profits are growing at a faster pace than expected.
Nippon Credit said it was also trying to deal with various other situations, taking into account uncertain factors such as movements in the stock market.
The bank said it also plans to carry out further restructuring by slashing the number of its workers and senior executives and by selling its real estate holdings.
"We have reported such bank efforts to the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Japan, so we are convinced that we will receive full support from the authorities," it said.
